column4: God knows which faction is most deserving of burning in Hell; this supplies the ص ل ي action immediately before 19:71's approach and 19:72's rescue of those who took protective heed.
Every person is brought to or passes over Hell before 19:72 distinguishes those God rescues for their taqwā, making divine removal from danger the climax of an actual approach to it.
Lezā is described as stripping away the skin or scalp, giving the named pure flame of 70:15 a bodily action before it calls the one who turned away in 70:17.
Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly consume fire into their bellies and will burn in a blaze, joining wrongful acquisition, internalized fire, and the section's ص ل ي action.
One who commits the prohibited act in aggression and injustice is promised admission to fire, another direct use of the section's burning-entry root with the conduct that leads there.
The skins of those burned in fire are repeatedly replaced so that they continue to taste punishment, concretizing the section's gloss of enduring the fire's heat and severity.
One who opposes the messenger after guidance is clear and follows another way is turned toward that choice and burned in Hell, directly joining a deviating route to fiery arrival.
Those who disbelieve and do wrong are denied guidance to a way, setting up 4:169's sole remaining path to Hell and tying rejection to misdirection.
The only path left to the deniers is the path of Hell, where they remain, closely paralleling the section's twisted course that terminates in fire.
The prayer says that whoever God admits into the fire is disgraced and has no helpers, clarifying admission as the opposite of being warded and moved aside.
The wicked burn in Hell on the Day of Judgment, using the section's ص ل ي root for their actual entry into fire.
They are never absent from that fire, adding the permanence contained in the section's explanation of entering and staying.
Whether the condemned endure patiently or not, the fire remains their dwelling and no appeal restores favor; this makes endurance powerless once the alarm has been ignored.
Messengers recount God's signs, and whoever takes protective heed and reforms has no fear; the ayah supplies the successful response before 7:36 gives the denier's fiery result.
Those who deny the signs and act arrogantly toward them become abiding companions of the fire, completing 7:35's warning-and-taqwā alternative.
The people are told to take protective heed of what lies before and behind them so that they may receive mercy, framing taqwā as spatial precaution against approaching danger.
No sign comes from their Lord without their turning away from it, supplying the failed response to the precautionary alarm in 36:45.

Abraham asks God to keep him and his children apart from idol worship; the causative form of ج ن ب shows divine distancing as protection, although the object avoided is an antecedent of punishment rather than the fire itself.
Every nation receives a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of false powers; warning and deliberate اجتناب are joined as the path of precaution.
Their sides leave their beds as they call on God in fear and hope and spend from His provision; the bodily “side” named in the shield gloss meets fear, action, and giving in one posture.
God says He will burn the rejecting man in Saqar, a direct use of the section's fire-entry root within the passage that later calls Saqar a warning to humanity.
Those who deny the Hour have a blaze prepared for them, placing denial of the warning's horizon immediately before the enraged fire that sees them from afar in 25:12.
The revelation warns the central city and those around it of the gathering day, when one group is in the Garden and another in the blaze; warning and the two destinations are stated together.
At the gathering, the people allied with jinn are assigned the fire as their abode; 6:130 later asks whether messengers warned them of this very meeting.

The gathered communities are asked whether messengers recited the signs and warned them of their meeting that day, and they testify against themselves; it supplies the acknowledged alarm behind 6:128's fire.
The polytheists call toward the fire whereas God calls toward the Garden and forgiveness, exposing two rival summons and the destination reached by answering each.
The oppressive leaders are made leaders who call people to the fire, a human counter-call to the warning voice that seeks to move hearers away from it.
The believing man asks why he calls his people to salvation while they call him to the fire, stating the section's opposed directions as rival spoken appeals.
Satan is an enemy whose party-call aims to make people companions of the blaze, joining the hostile threat, a summons, and fiery destination.
Those who practiced taqwā are conducted to the Garden in groups, forming the protected counterpart to the groups driven to Hell after their warning in 39:71-72.
God's kindled fire rises over the hearts, adding an inward reach to the hoarder's fire before 104:8 closes it over them.
The fire is closed over them in extended columns, completing the enclosure announced in 104:8 with the structure that seals it.

Those outside the wall are told that they tempted themselves, waited, doubted, and were deceived until God's command came, explaining the failed precaution that placed them on 57:13's punishment side.
The person whose refuge becomes Hell first transgresses, contributing the initiating act before 79:38 names preference for the nearer life and 79:39 names the fire.
Garments of fire are cut for the disbelieving party and boiling liquid is poured over their heads, turning an ordinarily protective layer into the punishment itself.
The poured heat melts what is inside their bellies and their skins, specifying the fire's severity before 22:22 describes their failed attempts to leave it.
Those who exchange God's favor for disbelief lead their people to ruin, Hell, which they enter and burn in; misdirection by a leader ends in the section's ص ل ي action.
The wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worship are gathered together before 37:23 directs them to Hell's path, supplying the company being marched toward that destination.
The messenger is asked whether he can rescue someone already in the fire after the sentence has taken effect; the impossible rescue contrasts with God's promised warding before entry.
One person is cast into the fire while another arrives secure on Resurrection Day, setting fiery admission and protected arrival side by side.

The expelled people thought their fortresses would protect them, but judgment reached them from where they did not expect; the failed external barrier clarifies why the section locates effective protection in taqwā and God's warding.

Those who keep themselves away from false powers and turn to God receive good news; their self-directed اجتناب shows the same distancing motion that the wretched misdirect toward the reminder in 87:11.
Joseph's interpretation instructs sustained sowing and protected storage before the announced famine, a specific nonlexical parallel to warning becoming complete through practical precaution.
The seven hard years then consume what was stored except a protected remainder, showing why the advance measures ordered in 12:47 constitute an effective shield.
The community is told to take protective heed of a trial that will not strike only the wrongdoers, extending taqwā from personal fear to precaution against a danger that can overrun a whole group.
Each soul is commanded to inspect what it has sent ahead for tomorrow while repeating the call to taqwā, explicitly making foresight and preparation the response to future danger.
Humbled faces burn in an intensely hot fire, a compact repeated formulation of the section's entry verb together with the heat it must endure.
The one receiving the record behind the back cries for destruction and burns in a blaze, another contextualized occurrence of the section's ص ل ي action.
Those veiled from their Lord then burn in Hell, using the same root for entry while adding exclusion from divine presence as the condition preceding it.
